# Widget `parameter-explorer` — Parameter explorer

**Pack:** math

**When to use:** Use for a formula with 1–4 inputs so the learner can move sliders and watch the results change.

## Example block

```json
{
  "kind": "widget",
  "type": "parameter-explorer",
  "title": "Parameter explorer",
  "props": {
    "inputs": [
      {
        "id": "m",
        "label": "Mass",
        "min": 1,
        "max": 100,
        "step": 1,
        "value": 10,
        "unit": "kg"
      },
      {
        "id": "v",
        "label": "Speed",
        "min": 0,
        "max": 30,
        "step": 0.5,
        "value": 5,
        "unit": "m/s"
      }
    ],
    "outputs": [
      {
        "label": "Kinetic energy",
        "expr": "0.5 * m * v^2",
        "unit": "J",
        "decimals": 1
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Props

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `inputs` | array of object (1–4) | yes |
| `inputs[].id` | string (pattern `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`) | yes |
| `inputs[].label` | string | yes |
| `inputs[].min` | number | yes |
| `inputs[].max` | number | yes |
| `inputs[].step` | number | yes |
| `inputs[].value` | number | yes |
| `inputs[].unit` | string | no |
| `outputs` | array of object (1–4) | yes |
| `outputs[].label` | string | yes |
| `outputs[].expr` | string | yes |
| `outputs[].unit` | string | no |
| `outputs[].decimals` | integer (≥ 0, ≤ 6) | no |

The validator also checks the cross-field rules (ids that must exist, lengths that must match,
expressions that must parse). Run `npm run validate` after writing a widget.
